$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. TransferEnvelope per LOOP_ENGINEERING_SPEC_V2.1.md §21 (Transfer and activation boundary): 'Transfer moves inert bytes. It does not grant authority, resolve secrets, or start execution... Every transfer is represented by a user-initiated envelope containing expected media type and digest.' This schema states the boundary object only — the full ten-step import grammar and eleven-state machine are LOOP_IMPORT_ACTIVATION_CONTRACT.md's (FB-RAT-IMP-001), not restated here.
title: TransferEnvelope
description: The user-initiated envelope that precedes any package transfer, carrying the transfer channel, the caller's EXPECTED media type and digest (checked against what actually arrives), and a human-readable source description. Typically carried as the `payload` of a ContractEnvelope<TransferEnvelope> (schemas/common/envelope.schema.json), inheriting objectId/createdAtUtc/producer from that outer envelope.

transferChannel.description: Matches the transfer channel enumeration LOOP_DUAL_SURFACE_ARCHITECTURE.md §7 lists as the canonical LoopPackage boundary crossings: a .floop file, the Android share sheet, a marketplace/unlisted release HTTPS URL, a QR code carrying a URL plus expected digest, or a user-owned Git repository.

expectedMediaType.description: IANA media type the caller expects the transferred bytes to be (e.g. 'application/zip' for a .floop archive). Checked against the actual container's declared/sniffed media type before any further processing — a mismatch is a rejection at the transfer boundary, before parsing begins (LOOP-PKG-004: import never executes package content, which presupposes the bytes are validated as the expected shape before anything touches them).

expectedDigest.description: The digest the caller expects the transferred bytes to hash to, known BEFORE the transfer completes (e.g. from a QR payload, a marketplace listing, or a prior handoff). Compared against the actually-received bytes' digest once the transfer completes; a mismatch is 'declared-digest / actual-digest mismatch', one of floop-container-format.v1.json's adversarialClasses_MUST_reject.

initiatedByUser.description: MUST-level invariant (LOOP_ENGINEERING_SPEC_V2.1 §21, FB-RAT-IMP-002): a TransferEnvelope only exists because a human took a transfer-initiating action. There is no representable 'false' value — a producer that cannot truthfully assert user initiation MUST NOT construct a TransferEnvelope at all; encoding this as `const: true` rather than a plain boolean makes 'this transfer was not user-initiated' unrepresentable in this object, not merely disallowed by convention.

sourceDescription.description: Human-readable description of where these bytes came from (e.g. 'QR code scanned from publisher listing', 'shared via WhatsApp', 'cloned from git@github.com:...'), surfaced to the user before any authority or binding controls are presented (LOOP_ENGINEERING_SPEC_V2.1 §21: 'Fonebrew snapshots the bytes, validates the container, and performs local compatibility evaluation before presenting authority or binding controls').
